summary: Arindam Chakrabarti is an Indologist and philosopher who earned a DPhil from the University of Oxford. He has held professorships at the University of Delhi, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Stony Brook University as Mattoo Endowed Chair.
Arindam Mondal is an Indologist who earned an M.Phil. from Jadavpur University and serves as an Assistant Professor at Shishuram Das College.
Arinde L. Jonker is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who earned a Research MA at Leiden University, studying under Peter C. Bisschop, Daniele Cuneo, and Jonathan A. Silk.
Arion Roşu (1924–2007) studied at the University of Bucharest from 1945 to 1950 and later at the University of Paris under Jean Filliozat from around 1965 to 1974.

Aristotle C. Dy is a scholar in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned PhDs from Ateneo de Manila University and SOAS University of London under Antonello Palumbo. He has served as Xavier School President and Ateneo lecturer.
Aritri Dutta is an external PhD researcher in Tibetology and religious studies at Leiden University under the supervision of Henk Blezer.

Arjo Vanderjagt is a philosopher who studied at the University of Groningen between 1971 and 1981. He later held academic posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), Utrecht University (2007), and the University of Groningen (1994–2009).

Arjuna S. R. works in computational linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Karnataka Samskrit University and the University of Hyderabad (PhD 2012–2017), he served as Senior Research Coordinator and later Assistant Registrar at Manipal Academy of Higher Education.

Arlo Griffiths is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and archaeology who earned his PhD at Leiden University under Henk Bodewitz. He has held professorships at Leiden University and the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Indologist Armand Guérinot (1872–1940) studied under Paul Regnaud at the University of Lyon, where he earned his Ph.D., and under Hermann Jacobi at the University of Bonn. In 1909, he worked at the Imprimerie Nationale.

Armand Minard (1906–1998) was a French Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Paris. He held academic posts at the University of Lyon (1933–1957), École Pratique des Hautes Études (1952–1976), and the Sorbonne (1957–1977).

Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval (1795–1871) was a linguist who served as Professor of Vulgar Arabic at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1821–1871) and Professor of Arabic at the Collège de France (1833–1871).
Armin W. Geertz is a religious studies scholar who spent his academic career at Aarhus University, where he became Professor Emeritus in 2019.

Arnab Bhattacharya works in computational fields and Indology. Educated at IIT Bombay and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (Ph.D. 1997), he has held posts at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Homi Bhabha Centre, and IIT Kanpur.

Arnaldo Beltrami (b. 1862) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Turin. He taught at Liceo Ginnasio Luigi Galvani (1896–1931) and was a Docent of Greek at the University of Bologna.
Arnav Anjaria is a scholar in Tibetology who studied at the University of Hyderabad (2007–2014) and served as an Assistant Professor at Amity University from 2018 to 2019.

Arnold Adriaan Bake (1899–1963) studied Indology and religious studies at Leiden, Visva-Bharati, and Utrecht University under Willem Caland. He held research positions at Leiden and Brasenose College, and became a Lecturer at SOAS in 1948.
Arnold C. Taylor (1867–1955) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed an M.A. at the University of Oxford around 1890 and taught at Uppingham School from around 1891 to 1925.

Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren (1760–1842) was a German historian who earned his doctorate at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne. He spent his career at Göttingen, eventually becoming an ordentlicher Professor of History in 1801.
Arnold Hirzel (1861–1931) was an Indologist who studied at the universities of Strasbourg, Munich, and Leipzig, completing his Ph.D. at Leipzig around 1890 under Ernst Windisch.
